trends.title: Google Kills Doppl, Folds Virtual Try-On Directly Into Search and Shopping Results
trends.summary: On April 30, 2026, Google shut down its experimental Doppl virtual try-on app — not because it failed, but because the technology graduated into the core product. Users can now tap 'Try It On' directly on any apparel product listing or image result within Google Search, putting AI-powered VTON in front of hundreds of millions of shoppers without a separate app. Launch partners include Zalando, Zara, and L'Agence, signalling enterprise-grade retail adoption at Google scale.
trends.glance_relevance: Glance's own VTON feature (powered by Gemini + Imagen) is now validated at the highest level — Google itself is canonising virtual try-on as a default commerce surface. This directly supports Glance's thesis that AI-native try-on belongs embedded in ambient discovery surfaces (lockscreen, feed) rather than as a standalone destination. Strong editorial angle: 'The try-on era just became the default era.'

trends.title: BigCommerce Commerce Live 2026: Merchants' Product Feeds Now Pushed to ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Stripe as Agentic Commerce Goes Mainstream
trends.summary: At Commerce Live 2026 in Chicago (April 28–30), BigCommerce announced that its Feedonomics Surface product now syndicates merchant product data to AI discovery surfaces — ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, PayPal, and Stripe — turning AI chat interfaces into live storefronts. The company also launched BigCommerce Companion (an AI merchant assistant) and conversational search for storefronts, completing an end-to-end agentic commerce stack for mid-market and enterprise retailers.
trends.glance_relevance: BigCommerce syndicating to Gemini is directly adjacent to Glance's own Gemini-powered agent stack. The move confirms that product discovery is fracturing away from traditional search toward AI-native surfaces — precisely the ambient/lockscreen layer Glance already occupies. This is a strong 'Tech Depth' data point on how the agentic product-feed infrastructure is maturing and commoditising.

trends.title: Visa Q2 FY2026 Earnings: Agentic Commerce Named Next Growth Engine as Visa CLI and Agent-Ready Tokenisation Roll Out
trends.summary: In its April 28 earnings call, Visa management explicitly cited agentic commerce — where software agents initiate and complete transactions with minimal human intervention — as the company's next major growth engine. Visa revealed it had launched Visa CLI (a proof-of-concept letting developers pay for APIs via Visa credentials from the command line) and is expanding its 'Agentic Ready' program to Latin America and Asia. Revenue grew 17% YoY to $11.2B for the March quarter, with tokenisation and credential management flagged as the infrastructure layer underpinning agent transactions.
trends.glance_relevance: Visa naming agentic commerce as a core growth engine on a public earnings call is a landmark moment for the category — and a major credibility signal for Glance's own agentic commerce positioning. For the 'Market Intelligence' pillar, this is wall-street-grade validation that agentic commerce is moving from experiment to payment-rail infrastructure. Glance's D0 shopping feed and chat agent flows will ultimately route through exactly this kind of tokenised, agent-ready credential layer.

trends.title: Mastercard Q1 2026: 'Agent Pay' Advances and BVNK Stablecoin Acquisition Signals Payments Infrastructure Racing to Serve AI Agents
trends.source: Payment Expert / Motley Fool Earnings Transcript
trends.summary: Mastercard reported April 30 Q1 2026 earnings (revenue +12% to $8.4B) and used the call to advance its 'Agent Pay' capability — purpose-built payment rails for AI agent transactions — alongside announcing the acquisition of BVNK, a stablecoin infrastructure company. Together these moves show the payments duopoly racing to be the default settlement layer for autonomous AI commerce, a dynamic that will define the entire agentic commerce stack for the next decade.
trends.glance_relevance: With both Visa and Mastercard reporting on the same week and both flagging agentic commerce as core strategy, this is a once-in-a-cycle 'payments infrastructure is ready' signal. For Glance, whose agentic chat and D0 feed need frictionless one-tap checkout, having Visa and Mastercard actively building agent-native payment rails is the enabling infrastructure layer that makes agentic commerce at lockscreen-scale viable. Strong 'Tech Depth' pairing piece alongside the Visa story.

trends.title: Samsung Mobile Posts First-Ever Net Loss Warning as AI Memory Costs Soar — The Hidden Cost of the OEM AI Race
trends.summary: Samsung's MX (Mobile Experience) division head TM Roh warned leadership on April 27 that the smartphone business faces its first-ever net loss in 2026, as AI-driven DRAM and NAND demand from data centres is squeezing smartphone component margins to a historic extreme. LPDDR5x RAM — standard in AI-capable Android flagships — now competes directly with AI server demand, pushing memory costs above 20% of premium device BOM. Samsung has already raised Galaxy A-series and Z-series prices by $50–$80.
trends.glance_relevance: This story sits directly at the intersection of Glance's two key OEM partners: Samsung and Motorola (Lenovo). The cost squeeze is forcing OEMs to monetise their device real estate more aggressively — which makes pre-installed, revenue-generating AI surfaces like Glance's lockscreen commerce layer more strategically valuable, not less. OEMs under margin pressure become stronger Glance partners. This is a sharp 'Market Intelligence' angle: the same AI wave creating Glance's opportunity is also restructuring OEM economics in Glance's favour.
